entry.title: Next summit will be in Sydney! Meet its co-chairs
entry.content:
We are thrilled to announce our co-chairs, Martin Dehnel-Wild and Lucy Fletcher, for the seL4 summit 2027, which will be held in Sydney, 21 - 23 September 2027 (Dates TBC).

  • Martin Dehnel-Wild

    Chief Scientist, Kry10

    Dr Martin Dehnel-Wild is Chief Scientist of Kry10, where he leads R&D and heads up Kry10’s UK & European office. He has a DPhil (PhD) in Computer Science from the University of Oxford, where he researched interactive and automated theorem proving for security protocols. Prior to Kry10 he set up and led the UK Government’s formal methods (“provable security”) team, bringing rigorous, automated assurance tooling and techniques to the UK’s most critical and highest security systems. Most of his work over the last 10+ years has focused on pulling formal-methods based tools for software, hardware, and cryptography through to use by regular developers, promoting uptake and use across industry, government, and academia.

  • Lucy Fletcher

    Software Engineer, Apple

    Lucy Fletcher is a software engineer at Apple based in Sydney, Australia, working on L4 microkernels and the surrounding ecosystems. Before joining Apple, she studied Computer Science at UNSW and worked with the Trustworthy Systems group, where she focused on the design and development of the seL4 device driver framework. Lucy is passionate about giving back to the seL4 community and supporting its continued growth.

We look forward to welcoming the community at the seL4 summit 2027!

Stay tuned by following us on LinkedIn or subscribing to the RSS for our News page.

entry.title: New seL4 release available
entry.content:
We’re pleased to announce the release of

  • seL4 17.0.0: The seL4 microkernel
  • Microkit 2.4.0: The seL4 Microkit for building static-architecture systems
  • CAmkES 3.13.1: Component Architecture for microkernel-based Embedded Systems
  • capDL 0.6.1: Tools for generating, parsing and loading capability distribution specifications
  • rust-sel4 6.0.0: Rust support for seL4 userspace. See the Rust section on the seL4 docsite for more information.

This release focussed on fixing issues in unverified configurations of seL4, as well as auditing code in verified configurations that is not covered by the scope of seL4’s formal proofs. Like previous releases, this release contains security relevant changes and we recommend upgrading to the latest version of seL4.

We would like to thank Anthropic for reporting a number of these issues and for the constructive, actionable and useful way they were communicated. Overall, this audit has strengthened the security of seL4 in all parts of the kernel that the formal proofs do not make guarantees about.

seL4 17.0.0 and the corresponding Rust support have breaking changes and will require updates if you are using the seL4 API directly. The CAmkES and capDL tool releases are backwards compatible. The Microkit contains security and bug fixes and has breaking changes.

As always, a more detailed list of the changes and user-visible impact can be found in the seL4 release notes and the seL4 docsite, together with upgrade instructions.

Enjoy!

entry.title: The Australian National University joins seL4 Foundation
entry.content:
The seL4 Foundation is pleased to welcome the Australian National University (ANU) as an Associate Member. ANU's School of Computing has a longstanding connection to seL4, and ANU researchers have contributed to seL4's original verification efforts and DARPA's HACMS program.

This research contribution continues to grow through a broader concentration of formal methods and programming-languages expertise at ANU. Current work involves the development of programming languages for use with the seL4 Microkit.

The membership strengthens active collaborations between ANU's School of Computing and fellow Australian-based member organisations on the development of secure technology based on the seL4 ecosystem.

entry.title: seL4 security proofs now complete on AArch64
entry.content:
The verification of seL4 on the 64-bit Arm architecture has reached another milestone. After completing the proofs of functional correctness and integrity, Proofcraft has now established the proof that seL4 enforces confidentiality on AArch64, providing a formal mathematical proof that the kernel prevents an application running on top of seL4 from learning information without authorisation.

This milestone completes the formal proof that the seL4 implementation code on AArch64 enforces security isolation of the applications running on top (under the assumptions listed here). This isolation prevents attacks on non-critical applications from propagating to critical applications and compromising them.

entry.title: Thank you UNSW Sydney, bronze sponsor of the seL4 Summit 2026
entry.content:
The seL4 Foundation thanks UNSW Sydney for becoming a Bronze sponsor of the seL4 Summit 2026.

seL4 was created by the Trustworthy Systems (TS) team, which is now part of the UNSW, a founding member of the seL4 Foundation.

The team has a track record of designing and implementing systems software for performance and reliability, and using rigorous formal methods to prove that they meet their security and reliability goals. Their aims are to:

  • shift the software industry away from ad-hoc, unreliable engineering practices, and towards more principled and trustworthy methods; and
  • make verified software a default choice, especially in safety- and security-critical systems.

The team works with government and commercial partners, as well as the broader software engineering community, to drive this change.

entry.title: Happy seL4 day!
entry.content:
On July 29, 2009, the last "sorry" of the seL4 functional correctness proof was eliminated. A "sorry" is an assumed theorem lacking a complete proof. "0 sorries" meant there was nothing left to prove: the project was finished. We now celebrate this day every year to mark the seL4 day, when the world's first formally verified kernel with a machine-checked code-level proof came into existence.

On July 29, 2014, "seL4 day" became a double-celebratory day: the seL4 code and proofs became open source, paving the way to the widespread use it enjoys today.

A big thank-you to all for your continued support!

Learn more about the history of seL4.

entry.title: New seL4 release available
entry.content:
We’re pleased to announce the release of

  • seL4 16.0.0: The seL4 microkernel
  • Microkit 2.3.0: The seL4 Microkit for building static-architecture systems
  • CAmkES 3.13.0: Component Architecture for microkernel-based Embedded Systems
  • capDL 0.6.0: Tools for generating, parsing and loading capability distribution specifications
  • rust-sel4 5.0.0: Rust support for seL4 userspace. See the Rust section on the seL4 docsite for more information.

seL4 16.0.0 and the corresponding Rust support have breaking changes and will require updates if you are using the seL4 API directly. CAmkES and the capDL tool add units for domain schedules as a new feature, but are backwards compatible. The Microkit release comes with new features and has breaking changes for x86_64 systems.

Enjoy!
